A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeanAgent, with matching methods, repositories, and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the added Appendix A.7 in v7.

before.justification: V1 reports original theorem-proving experiments across 23 Lean repositories, lifelong-learning measurements, seven-variant ablations, and generated proof examples.

after.justification: V7 retains these original experiments and additionally reports a Lean4 MiniF2F test-set evaluation of LeanAgent and ReProver in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The proof-length curriculum, dynamic database, single-epoch progressive retriever training, and best-first proof search remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies embedding refreshes before validation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 23 repositories, curricula, and alternate PFR commit. The added MiniF2F test-set experiment changes the split and protocol within existing coverage. ProofNet and PutnamBench were not evaluated in v1, so deleting their exclusion discussion does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: ReProver and the same seven lifelong-learning variants remain the evaluated comparators. V7 also uses ReProver for its new MiniF2F protocol. TheoremLlama and DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 scores are discussed as external context with comparability qualifications; Aesop is explicitly not evaluated.

E3.justification: V1's main comparison uses TPPS with X = 10 and improvement ratios; v7 replaces this with direct proof counts and relegates TPPS to a qualified alternative in Appendix A.7. V7 also adds a separate 244-theorem MiniF2F test evaluation using Pass@1 and explicitly excludes Test.lean from progressive training, while retaining the earlier combined-split experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 extends the existing PFR case analysis by diagnosing two reflexivity proofs as artifacts of an unfinished multiDist definition. V7 also removes the one-line versus 175-line human-proof comparison for Wedderburn. The seven-variant ablations and most proof case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for the experiments. Both retain the same informal 3% threshold for calling an improvement significant; v7 adds no statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: The headline 162 proofs becomes 155 proofs plus seven exploits, a reclassification rather than demonstrated performance deterioration. TPPS scores and improvement ratios are replaced by proof counts and stage breakdowns. V7 adds separate MiniF2F test results of 38.1% (93/244) for LeanAgent versus 34.0% (83/244) for ReProver; the earlier 99-versus-85 result and lifelong-learning ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 qualifies the mathematical reasoning behind two PFR reflexivity proofs: their success depends on multiDist being an unfinished sorry definition, rather than establishing the intended distribution identities. The displayed proof scripts, complexity measure, EWC objective, and TPPS formula otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the achievement from 162 theorems previously unproved by humans to 155 previously unproved formally, with seven exploits identified separately. The headline 'up to 11 times' superiority claim is withdrawn, and identifying repository exploits becomes an explicit contribution. The central lifelong-learning claim remains.

C2.justification: PFR placeholder successes are reinterpreted as exploits rather than evidence of deep mathematical understanding. New Appendix A.7 discusses arbitrary TPPS weighting, inflated scores, repository loopholes, and unreliable proof-length proxies for difficulty. V7 also moderates several case-study interpretations and removes the claimed human-proof-length advantage.

D1.justification: New Table 9 documents theorem and premise totals, including dependencies, for each repository. Appendix A.2 clarifies that the reported 4-to-9-day runtime applies to the Table 10 experiments. Hardware, optimization settings, repository commits, and core implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: V7 adds the TheoremLlama reference and removes the ProofNet and PutnamBench references alongside their exclusion rationale. Added discussion positions LeanAgent relative to TheoremLlama, DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5, and Aesop, emphasizing lifelong learning and limits on direct comparisons. The broader related-work account remains intact.

P1.justification: The overall section structure is retained. V7 revises headline wording and case-study language, clarifies embedding updates, corrects 'Matrix Workshop' to 'Math Workshop,' and moves TPPS exposition into the expanded Appendix A.7. Most methodology and lifelong-learning analysis prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially redesigned from two TPPS columns into proof totals and learning-stage breakdowns, and a repository-statistics table is added. Figure 2 is rearranged and removes the PFR reflexivity example, which remains in Appendix A.5. Numerous appendix proof images are resized and repaginated without changing their contents; Table 4 gains metric-direction arrows.

improvement.justification: V7 substantially improves the credibility of the empirical claims by withdrawing the weighted '11 times' headline, separating seven exploits from the claimed proof total, explaining evaluation limitations, and adding a held-out MiniF2F comparison. These changes address central weaknesses in v1's evidence and interpretation. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 2 includes two acknowledged exploits and contradicts Appendix A.5 about Coxeter's learning-stage timing, but these issues do not outweigh the gains.
